Urethane grout is a close second. It shares the water-resistance and flexibility of epoxy but is easier to mix and clean. It’s also softer on your tools and your patience. If you’re dead set on sticking with epoxy, I’d grab a pre-mixed two-part system from a reputable brand like Laticrete or Mapei, and make sure you have the right sponges and a bucket of warm water nearby. Work in small sections, wipe the haze off frequently, and keep the sponge almost dry when you’re close to the cure time.

If you’re leaning toward urethane, the same brands carry those as well, and you’ll want to follow their curing schedule so you don’t get a cloudy film on the tile.
